newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais expected to join Russian govt - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Chubais expected to join Russian govt - newspaper.

text.p: Kremlin chief of staff Anatoly Chubais, an instigator of market reforms in Russia, is expected to return to the government to take charge of the economy, a liberal newspaper said on Wednesday.

The daily Sevodnya said President Boris Yeltsin and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin had agreed at talks on Tuesday to make Chubais, 41, the only first deputy prime minister under a cabinet reshuffle they are working on.

Presidential spokesmen have declined to say who might be promoted or fired. But Kremlin sources say Chubais, a liberal economist, is widely expected to be given responsibility for tackling economic problems.

"Anatoly Chubais' stepping into the role of first deputy prime minister, on which Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin agreed yesterday, will mean an abrupt change in the organisation of duties and functional links in the cabinet," Sevodnya said.
Sevodnya did not identify its sources for the report, which said Finance Minister Alexander Livshits would be dismissed.
A presidential spokesman said on Tuesday that Yeltsin had approved proposals by Chernomyrdin for changes in the government but gave no details.
The reshuffle is expected to be announced sometime after Yeltsin delivers a keynote speech to parliament on Thursday. The government is due to meet soon after the speech.

Yeltsin demanded changes after criticising the government's social policies, although the shake-up also appears to be part of efforts to reassert his authority following his long absences from the Kremlin with health problems.
The cabinet has three first deputy prime ministers, but Sevodnya said these three men would be demoted to underline Chubais' authority.
The ginger-haired Chubais was credited with masterminding Yeltsin's successful re-election campaign last year and is regarded as a talented organiser and administrator.

He is hated by the opposition communists and many ordinary Russians because of the much-criticised privatisation campaign he oversaw in an earlier spell in the cabinet, of which he was a member between 1991 and January last year.
But Chubais is admired by the likes of the International Monetary Fund and the Group of Seven industrial nations.
